title: SESH
summary: A responsive exercise and fitness tracking web app built on the MERN stack.
description: A full-stack application for logging workouts, tracking sessions and reviewing exercise history.
Authentication combines Passport, Google OAuth 2.0 and JWTs, with bcryptjs for password hashing.

The React frontend uses Redux Toolkit to manage workout data and React Router for navigation. React Hook Form handles form state and validation, while react-day-picker and date-fns support date selection and formatting.
The interface combines Radix UI primitives and shadcn-style components with Tailwind CSS.
An Express API and Mongoose handle the backend and database layer, with Resend providing transactional email.

title: LinkStore
summary: A tag-based bookmarking app built with Next.js and React for organising useful links into a searchable resource library.
description: Users save and organise links with custom tags, creating a personal resource library without relying on folders or crowded bookmark bars.
Built with Next.js 16 and React 19, with MongoDB and Mongoose providing the data layer.
Authentication uses NextAuth with the MongoDB adapter and bcryptjs for password hashing. A custom password reset flow uses secure database tokens and reset links delivered through Resend.
The interface combines Radix UI primitives and shadcn-style components with Tailwind CSS, Lucide icons, Sonner notifications and Vaul drawers.
MDX supports rich, formatted content alongside saved resources. The application is written in JavaScript.

title: Scroll
summary: A minimalist note-taking app built with Django, with custom tags and a calm, focused interface.
description: A note-taking application built with Django 6, designed around a clean interface for writing and organising notes with tags.
Supabase-hosted PostgreSQL provides the relational database, with environment-based configuration and a local SQLite fallback for development.
Authentication uses django-allauth for login, registration, password resets and Google OAuth.
Django templates and django-widget-tweaks provide control over form rendering without introducing a separate frontend framework.
Deployed on Render, with Gunicorn serving the application and WhiteNoise handling static assets.

title: ePianos
summary: A custom WooCommerce theme and supporting tools for a live UK piano retailer.
description: A custom-built e-commerce theme focused on lightweight pages, responsive navigation and a product experience tailored to the retailer.
Product pages feature a custom layout and gallery, Ajax add-to-cart and dynamic add-on modules for related accessories. Custom fields control product videos and alternative product suggestions.
A searchable video library brings internally produced reviews, demonstrations and tutorials together within the site.
A custom search plugin serves both the public website and an admin-only knowledge base. It uses a dedicated REST endpoint and custom SQL, with tag-based weighting to improve result relevance.
Bespoke landing-page forms and a custom modal plugin support specific workflows, alongside Gravity Forms and WP Rocket.

title: Mapper
summary: A delivery quotation tool that calculates road distance and pricing from a UK address or postcode.
description: Built for an instrument retailer, Mapper lets staff search for a UK address or postcode, view its location on a map and generate an estimated delivery price from the showroom.
Google Places provides address autocomplete, while a Next.js API route contacts the Distance Matrix API using a server-side API key.
Delivery prices come from a local JSON file of fixed mileage bands, avoiding the need for a database. The origin postcode is configurable through an environment variable.
A responsive, full-screen map supports floating search and quotation panels. React state manages the selected location, loading indicators, errors and quotation results.

title: Blockader
summary: An experimental WordPress block theme exploring bold typography, custom blocks and Full Site Editing.
description: A stripped-back block theme built to explore modern WordPress development through custom templates, template parts and pattern-driven layouts.
Global styles are managed through theme.json, including responsive typography, spacing and theme-aware CSS variables.
A dynamic banner block provides editable content and button colour controls, with PHP rendering the frontend.
A live search block uses debounced requests to the WordPress REST API to display matching posts and pages.
An associated posts block presents related content with featured images, post type labels and responsive card layouts.
demoNote: This is a static demonstration. Live REST search requires a running WordPress backend and is unavailable here.

title: dbwp.pro
summary: A responsive landing-page concept for WordPress services, built with Next.js and Tailwind CSS.
description: A design proof of concept exploring bold visuals, clear service descriptions and straightforward navigation for a WordPress services website.
The page combines an introductory hero, service cards, a sample project gallery and an enquiry form.
Six fictional projects demonstrate the gallery layout, with each opening a modal containing an image, summary and placeholder project links.
Reusable React components handle the gallery, modal, mobile menu and contact form. Lucide icons and subtle Motion animations provide interface detail.
The form connects to Formspree without a separate backend. Written in JSX with Next.js App Router and Tailwind CSS, the site is deployed as a static build.
demoNote: A design proof of concept. Gallery projects are fictional and their destination links are placeholders.

title: Vaultage
summary: A customisable cloud file storage application built with Express and Supabase.
description: A cloud storage project exploring a customisable alternative to services such as Dropbox and Google Drive.
A Node.js and Express backend uses Supabase for both PostgreSQL data and file storage, with Prisma providing the database access layer.
Multer handles file uploads, while Zod validates incoming data before it reaches the database.
Authentication uses JWTs and password hashing to control access to file management features.
Registration and login flows are implemented, while the live demonstration provides a preconfigured demo login so visitors can try the interface without creating an account.
demoNote: The Supabase database may be paused, temporarily preventing access.

title: Ecom
summary: A bespoke WooCommerce block theme with a bold visual identity and a custom REST-powered contact form.
description: A modern WooCommerce demonstration theme combining vivid orange accents, neutral surfaces and typography-led layouts.
Custom block templates use native WordPress and WooCommerce blocks to shape the storefront, product pages, search, cart and checkout.
A custom contact-form block provides an editor preview and a PHP-rendered, accessible frontend form, compiled using WordPress Scripts.
A dedicated view.js submits the form asynchronously to a custom WordPress REST API endpoint, with honeypot spam protection, validation feedback and an accessible status area.
demoNote: This is a static demonstration. WooCommerce transactions and server-side form submissions are unavailable.

title: David Brandon / Dev
summary: A custom WordPress portfolio presenting my development work through a precise, typography-led interface.
description: A bespoke WordPress block theme built around a clinical visual style: bold typography, fine borders, neutral surfaces and orange accents.
Custom templates and template parts define the layout, with theme.json providing shared colours, font families, typography and spacing presets.
A responsive project grid opens reusable native dialog modals populated from a local JSON file, bringing together project descriptions, technology stacks, video demonstrations and source links.
A separate profile modal introduces my commercial background, while a Formspree contact form provides a direct enquiry route.
Typed.js, AOS scroll animations and a CSS code-rain effect add movement. Frontend JavaScript and library styles are bundled using WordPress Scripts.
